first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and two inherited records bear directly on it: memory_31 (cutting required signup fields produced a durable SMB activation lift) and memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value but increased early churn in complex-workspace accounts). Simplifying onboarding for self-serve/SMB, with the full flow preserved for complex workspaces, is the single action that attacks both declines while respecting the known segment boundary. I decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 says it buys acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it, which is directly opposed to the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective; reacting to a competitor is exactly the pressure that would tempt me to overwrite that caveat. Referral incentive (memory_57) is sound but targets established customers, not the failing funnel stage. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the closest runner-up but its recorded outcome is week-one engagement, an upstream proxy, with no evidence it moves retained revenue. I spend both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the load-bearing ones: from memory_86 I need the actual definition of 'complex workspace' and the magnitude/timing of the churn effect, since my whole guard depends on drawing that exclusion line correctly; from memory_31 I need to know whether the 'durable lift' was measured on activation only or followed through to retained revenue, and how old and how large the sample was. Key downstream risk I am explicitly flagging: both supporting memories report funnel-stage proxies (completion, activation, first-week action), not long-run qualified revenue. A faster funnel can admit lower-intent accounts, so an activation win could show up as flat or negative revenue a quarter out; that is the same failure mode memory_73 already documents for pricing. I am therefore running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: hard-exclude complex-workspace accounts, hold out a control, and pre-commit to 30-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-signup as gating metrics rather than judging on completion rate alone. If verification contradicts either memory, I will fall back to activation_messaging rather than proceeding on unverified ground.

final.rationale: Both pulls confirmed the inherited summaries and sharpened the guard, so I am committing the slot to simplify_onboarding, scoped to SMB self-serve accounts with complex-workspace accounts hard-excluded and left on the full flow. exp_31 is the strongest record in the inventory for my actual objective: it does not stop at a funnel proxy but carries through to qualified revenue +4% on SMB, with 30-day retention only -1%. That resolves the main worry I flagged before verification, that a faster funnel would just admit lower-intent accounts. exp_86 confirms the segment boundary is real and gives me the mechanism: the shortened flow deletes setup steps complex workspaces actually need, and the +9% churn is concentrated there. A mechanism-level explanation is much more transportable than a bare correlation, so I trust the exclusion to hold. Two things verification changed rather than merely confirmed. First, exp_86's harm shows up at 60 days, not 30, so a 30-day readout would have called this clean while the damage was still forming; I am setting the primary gate at 60 days and treating any 30-day result as provisional. Second, exp_31's conclusion says explicitly 'not replicated on other segments,' so the +4% qualified revenue is an SMB fact, not a company-wide fact, and I will not let a good SMB readout justify widening to mid-market or enterprise without a fresh test. I continue to decline promotional_pricing even though it is the direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records strong acquisition bought with a material 30-day retention loss and warns against generalizing it, which is the opposite of sustainable qualified revenue. Competitive pressure is precisely the condition under which I would be tempted to discount that caveat, so I am holding it. Simplify_onboarding also happens to be a partial answer to the same pressure, since it improves self-serve time-to-value without discounting the product. Residual uncertainty I am carrying forward rather than resolving: exp_31 and exp_86 are day-24 and day-52 records, and the current -6% activation and -4% completion declines may have a cause those experiments never probed, such as a product or pricing-page change, in which case re-simplifying treats a symptom. So this runs as a guarded test with a holdout, not a rollout: SMB self-serve only, complex workspaces excluded by explicit workspace-complexity criteria drawn from the exp_86 record, gated on 60-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-signup, with completion and activation as secondary reads only. If 60-day retention degrades or qualified revenue is flat, I stop and write that back to memory rather than reinterpreting the completion lift as success. Activation_messaging (memory_91) remains the fallback for the next slot; its recorded outcome is week-one engagement only, an upstream proxy with no revenue follow-through, which is why it loses to the revenue-confirmed option this week.
